title: AI Activate 2026 — Addressing Bias
category: AI Activate 2026 · Addressing Bias in Intelligent Systems

questions.q: ProPublica's analysis of the COMPAS recidivism tool found it was most likely to:
options: Falsely flag Black defendants as future criminals at nearly twice the rate of white defendants
Refuse to score anyone under 25
Only ever agree with the judge's own decision
Score all defendants as low-risk to stay safe
questions.why: COMPAS reproduced patterns in historical arrest data — the false-positive rate for Black defendants was roughly double that of white defendants, even though the model never saw race directly.

questions.q: Amazon scrapped its experimental AI recruiting tool because it:
options: Was too slow to score CVs
Penalised CVs containing the word “women's” and downgraded female candidates
Could only read PDFs
Recommended only external hires
questions.why: Trained on ten years of mostly-male CVs, the model learned that male-associated language signalled a strong candidate — a textbook case of historical bias baked into training data.

questions.q: When credit-scoring models “bake in” past discrimination, the core mechanism is:
options: Random noise in the data
A bug in the scoring code
Historical inequality encoded in the training data being learned and repeated
Too few variables in the model
questions.why: If the past outcomes a model learns from were shaped by discrimination, an accurate model faithfully reproduces that discrimination — accuracy and fairness are not the same thing.

questions.q: Under the EU AI Act, systems like CV-screening and credit-scoring are generally classified as:
options: Minimal-risk, no obligations
Banned outright in all cases
High-risk, requiring oversight, documentation and risk management
Exempt because they are automated
questions.why: The Act uses risk tiers; decisions affecting access to employment or credit fall in the high-risk tier, which carries transparency, human-oversight and documentation duties.

questions.q: Research on gender bias in NLP found that simply swapping gendered words (lexical de-biasing):
options: Completely removes bias from the model
Does not fully remove it — bias persists in the learned structure and embeddings
Makes models refuse to run
Is only needed for images, not text
questions.why: Bias lives in the geometry of the embeddings and co-occurrence structure, not just surface words, so lexical substitution leaves much of it intact — a key reason de-biasing is hard.
